contenu.angle: A trending news event is turned into a quick numbered rundown of 3 facts, a myth-busting explanation, a personal verdict on the most surprising one, and a question for the audience.
contenu.transformation: Pick a real trending news cluster with 2-3 related events. Open with a curious why-question about the most surprising one. Give each event as a numbered fact with one key number and one place. Add a one-line plain-language explanation that clears up a confusing detail. Link the events with a common theme, pick your own most surprising item, then ask which one the viewer saw first. Use fresh wording and your own verdict, never the source's phrasing.

structure.pattern: Why-question about the odd or surprising side of a news event
structure.example: Why did a storm in one country knock out power in its neighbor too?

structure.pattern: Fact #1: 'Reports say' plus the key number, place and the surprising reach
structure.example: Reports say a magnitude 6.1 tremor hit Chile, and people felt it across the mountains.

structure.pattern: Short explanation that makes the odd claim make sense
structure.example: It sounds strange, but waves travel through rock, not along maps.

structure.pattern: Fact #2: 'Meanwhile' plus number, place and the trending angle
structure.example: Meanwhile, a 4.9 tremor in Japan became a top search overnight.

structure.pattern: Fact #3: place plus number with a short punchy verb
structure.example: Near Greece, a magnitude 5.5 quake rattled the coast.

structure.pattern: Tie the facts together with a common theme in one line
structure.example: Three places, one lesson. The planet never really rests.

structure.pattern: 'My verdict?' plus the most surprising item and why
structure.example: My verdict? The first one is the wildest because the shaking ignored a border.

structure.pattern: Audience question followed by a follow-for-next-fact line
structure.example: Which one did you hear about first? Follow for the next fact.

script_style.tone: calm, curious, informative with a light conversational verdict

visuel.ambiance: Deep purple radial-gradient background with a soft glow in the center and slowly drifting golden sparkle particles. Bold yellow and white sans-serif text with a soft shadow.
visuel.scene_defaut: Dark purple vignette background with drifting small golden dots. A yellow rounded pill badge at the top holds the fact number. A big emoji or icon sits in the upper middle, and large bold word-by-word captions sit in the lower middle.

scenes.hook: Large question text in white with yellow keywords pops in on the purple sparkle background, with a small topic emoji or flag icons beside it. Gentle scale-in, then a hold.
scenes.setup: A yellow pill badge reading FACT #1 slides in at the top. Below it a flat newspaper icon with a globe floats and bobs gently. Yellow uppercase captions appear word by word near the lower middle. Keywords like REPORTS or the number pop in.
scenes.twist: The badge stays. A thinking-face emoji replaces the icon with a small wobble. Captions pop in word by word, alternating white and yellow for emphasis.
scenes.list_item: The badge changes to FACT #2. A small white spaced-caps label MAGNITUDE sits above a huge yellow number that counts up or punches in. A yellow jagged seismic waveform line runs horizontally under it and shimmers. A small caption repeats the number at the bottom.
scenes.escalation: The badge changes to FACT #3. The same number-and-waveform layout, with a new big number. A row beneath shows an emoji, a flag and the place name in white bold text. Captions pop in word by word.
scenes.payoff: A scales-of-justice emoji and the title MY VERDICT in white and yellow pop in at the top with a bounce. The lower captions follow the spoken words one by one, with the key word in yellow.
scenes.cta: Question text WHICH ONE DID YOU HEAR ABOUT FIRST? in white with yellow keywords at the top. Below it two flag emojis side by side, each with a yellow number label. Captions at the bottom, ending on a follow prompt.

audio.music_mood: Very quiet, soft ambient synth pad with a steady light pulse around 90 bpm, almost inaudible under the voice
sfx: soft pop on each caption word
whoosh when the fact badge changes
light ding on the verdict reveal

why_it_works: The numbered facts give a clear, easy-to-follow rhythm. The big numbers and badge stay in the same place, so the structure is instantly readable. The odd-claim explanation adds a small reward of understanding. The personal verdict and the closing question invite comments and follows with no cuts needed.
